subject: chemistry
source_material: ICSE Chemistry Paper-2 PPA-18 (Qualitative Analysis; year not stated in source)

canonical_criteria.requirement: Reagent added dropwise then to excess: report precipitate formation with colour AND its behaviour in excess reagent.
accepted_equivalents: white precipitate dissolves in excess NaOH
white ppt then clear colourless solution on excess
insufficient_alone: formula of the hydroxide in place of the word precipitate
mandatory_dependencies: both checkpoints required: (1) precipitate + colour, (2) transition in excess
recommended_not_required: name of the reagent added in excess

canonical_criteria.requirement: Gas/vapour liberated at an electrode: colour of the gas, the word vapour/gas, and the electrode.
accepted_equivalents: reddish brown vapour at the anode
reddish brown fumes at the anode
mandatory_dependencies: state word (vapour/gas) must accompany the colour
recommended_not_required: naming the electrode before the observation

canonical_criteria.requirement: Precipitate whose solubility changes with temperature: report precipitate colour AND the effect of heating on it.
required_anchors: effect of heating (dissolves / colourless solution on heating)
accepted_equivalents: white precipitate which dissolves on heating
initially white ppt, colourless solution on heating
insufficient_alone: white precipitate only (effect of heating omitted)
equation without colour of the precipitate
mandatory_dependencies: both the cold precipitate state and the hot state must be covered

canonical_criteria.requirement: Deliquescent solid exposed to air: solid absorbs moisture and turns into a (colourless) solution.
Double decomposition giving an insoluble salt: state that a precipitate forms AND its colour.
insufficient_alone: BaSO4 formed (word precipitate or colour missing)
mandatory_dependencies: word precipitate and colour both required

negative_constraints.context: Describing a white amphoteric hydroxide precipitate (e.g. Pb(OH)2) dissolving in excess alkali. Not applicable when describing the precipitate or a suspension itself, where white is correct.
Lead nitrate solution with NaOH added dropwise to excess. Not applicable to hydroxides that genuinely stay insoluble (e.g. Cu2+, Fe2+, Fe3+).

negative_constraints.correct_form: white precipitate soluble in excess of sodium hydroxide solution
negative_constraints.context: Q1(e)(i)-type dropwise-to-excess observation; a formula without precipitate/solubility information leaves the answer incomplete.

negative_constraints.wrong_form: colour given without the word vapour or gas
negative_constraints.context: Halogen/coloured gas liberated at an electrode.

negative_constraints.wrong_form: grey metal deposited at the anode
negative_constraints.correct_form: reddish brown vapour at the anode (lead is deposited at the cathode)
negative_constraints.context: Molten PbBr2 electrolysed with graphite electrodes; anode observation asked.

negative_constraints.wrong_form: chemical equation or formula written instead of an observation
negative_constraints.correct_form: sensory description (colour, precipitate, gas, odour, solubility)

negative_constraints.context: Pb(NO3)2 solution mixed with dilute HCl and heated; no NO2 is evolved in this reaction.

archetypes.name: Reason / Justification Questions
trigger_patterns: Give a reason for each of the following
Why is direct absorption ... not feasible

canonical_criteria.requirement: High melting point of ionic compounds: strong electrostatic force of attraction between oppositely charged ions.
accepted_equivalents: energy is required to separate ions held by strong electrostatic force

canonical_criteria.requirement: Inert gases do not form ions: stable electronic configuration, stated explicitly.
required_anchors: stable electronic configuration / complete outermost shell / 8 electrons in valence shell
accepted_equivalents: do not lose or gain electrons to form ions
insufficient_alone: inert gases are stable (configuration not mentioned)

canonical_criteria.requirement: Ionisation potential increases across a period: increasing nuclear charge and decreasing atomic size strengthen attraction on valence electrons in the same shell.
required_anchors: nuclear charge increases / atomic size decreases
accepted_equivalents: force of attraction on valence electrons increases

canonical_criteria.requirement: Alkali metals are good reducing agents: low ionisation potential / one valence electron, hence easy loss of electron.
required_anchors: low ionisation potential or one valence electron

canonical_criteria.requirement: Conductivity of dilute HCl exceeds that of acetic acid: comparative, covering BOTH acids (complete vs partial ionisation).
accepted_equivalents: HCl has higher concentration of ions
HCl has higher degree of dissociation
HCl only ions, acetic acid ions and molecules
insufficient_alone: statement about only one of the acids

canonical_criteria.requirement: Conc. H2SO4 not used to dry NH3: NH3 is basic and reacts with the acid to form ammonium sulphate.
required_anchors: NH3 reacts with conc. H2SO4 / forms ammonium sulphate
accepted_equivalents: NH3 being basic combines with conc. H2SO4

canonical_criteria.requirement: NH3 is not collected over water: highly soluble in water.
required_anchors: NH3 highly soluble / dissolves in water

canonical_criteria.requirement: Direct absorption of HCl in water is not feasible: back suction, because HCl dissolves faster than it is produced.
required_anchors: HCl dissolves faster than it is produced
insufficient_alone: HCl is highly soluble (back suction effect not mentioned)
mandatory_dependencies: the effect (back suction) must be stated

canonical_criteria.requirement: Apparatus for HNO3 preparation is all glass: HNO3 vapours are corrosive and attack rubber, cork.
required_anchors: HNO3 vapour corrosive / attacks rubber and cork / does not react with glass

negative_constraints.correct_form: strong electrostatic force of attraction between ions
negative_constraints.context: Explaining the high melting point of ionic compounds. Intermolecular forces are correct for molecular covalent substances.

negative_constraints.wrong_form: inert gases are stable (no electronic configuration)
negative_constraints.correct_form: stable electronic configuration / 8 electrons in valence shell
negative_constraints.context: Reason why inert gases do not form ions.

negative_constraints.wrong_form: describing conductivity of only HCl or only acetic acid
negative_constraints.context: Comparative conductivity of dilute HCl vs acetic acid.

negative_constraints.wrong_form: HCl is highly soluble (back suction not mentioned)
negative_constraints.correct_form: HCl dissolves faster than produced, causing back suction
negative_constraints.context: Why direct absorption of HCl in water is not feasible.

negative_constraints.wrong_form: rubber will melt due to heat / cork will break
negative_constraints.correct_form: nitric acid vapours are corrosive and attack rubber/cork
negative_constraints.context: Why apparatus for nitric acid preparation is entirely glass.

negative_constraints.wrong_form: reason for an increase/trend stated without cause (no nuclear charge / atomic size)
negative_constraints.correct_form: nuclear charge increases and size decreases

archetypes.name: Mole Concept, Stoichiometry and Gas Volumes

canonical_criteria.requirement: Empirical formula from percentage composition: atoms = % / atomic mass, divide by smallest, simplest whole-number ratio, formula in correct element order.

unresolved_anomalies.issue: Marking scheme Q4(b)(i) prints 'Mass of Al(OH)2' (typo); working 312/144 x 12 = 26 g is consistent with Al(OH)3.
unresolved_anomalies.reason: Text erratum in key; rubric uses Al(OH)3 and 26 g.

unresolved_anomalies.issue: Q4(b) is [4] marks with no printed split; rubric assumes 2 + 2 across (i) and (ii). Q4(a) [2] assumed as 1 ratio + 1 formula. Q6(b) [4] assumed 2 + 2.
unresolved_anomalies.reason: Unprinted multi-mark splits; the 3-mark (2+1) template in the prompt does not fit a 4-mark item.

unresolved_anomalies.issue: Examiner comment for Q5(b) labels the process answer '(i)' and the equation '(ii)', while the question has (i) ore, (ii) process, (iii) equation.
unresolved_anomalies.reason: Sub-part labels shifted; comments mapped to criteria by content.

unresolved_anomalies.issue: Q3(a)(i): examiners report NaOH or (NH4)2SO4 as incorrect choices, yet the paper note says alternate correct solutions were accepted and both routes are chemically valid.
unresolved_anomalies.reason: Examiner comment (rule 2) retained as a half-mark deduction; needs human decision on whether to accept valid alternatives.

unresolved_anomalies.issue: Key writes bare 'HCl' (Q1(c)(v)) and 'H2SO4' (Q7(b)(i)) while General Comments tell candidates to state acid strength.
unresolved_anomalies.reason: Strength requirement enforced only where it changes the answer (Q3(b)(i)); equations not penalised for omitting it.

unresolved_anomalies.issue: Key Q1(d)(ii) accepts condensed forms (CH3-CH2-CH2-CH3, H3C-CH(CH3)-CH3) as OR alternatives, whereas RULE_5 voids condensed formulas in 'draw the structure' questions.
